title: Supremum-Type Inference for Isotonic Observed Dose-Response Curves
banked_reason: The promised simultaneous LR calibration with an extreme-value/Poisson/Gumbel limit is replaced by an unconsumed open program; the retained scaling and action facts establish none of the advertised rate, limit-law, coverage, or calibrated-estimator objects.
gap_reasons: The promised Stat contribution—an evaluable simultaneous LR calibration with an extreme-value/Poisson/Gumbel limit—is replaced by an unconsumed open program; the retained scaling and action facts establish none of the Stat frontier objects (rate, limit law, coverage, or calibrated estimator).

The note does not deliver the advertised extreme-value calibration: it proves only finite-dimensional stationarity, scaling identities, a loose deterministic action bracket, an algebraic spatial clock, and deterministic profile inversion.
The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.
proof_attempt_summary: The run attempted to derive the canonical Brownian–GCM LR-energy excursion tail, additive ratio, cluster intensity, and Poisson/Gumbel limit needed for simultaneous causal-isotonic calibration. Primary-source comparison and high-reasoning review showed that fixed-location LR and argmax/slope-error extreme-value results do not transfer to this nonlocal LR-energy field; the missing Palm/LDP, anticlustering, grid, and statistical-coupling theory is genuine new research. The final honest graph retains an exact random-diagonal nonidentification witness, finite-dimensional stationarity, scaling identities, a 1/2-to-9/8 action bracket, spatial-clock algebra, and deterministic inversion, but not the promised calibrated band.
tldr: Proposition \(\texttt{prop:exact-dose-nonidentification}\) proves, by two explicit random-diagonal full-data extensions of one observed law, that the frozen assumptions do not identify \(\mathbb E[Y(a)]\) at any deterministic dose. The paper therefore targets only the observed-law curve \(\theta(a)=\int m(a,w)p(w)\,dw\). On the likelihood-ratio side, the proved content is fixed-location finite-dimensional stationarity; exact Brownian scaling, which by itself gives no large-deviation principle or tail law; the proved deterministic action bracket \(1/2\le I_\star\le9/8\) with its single-plateau witness; the exact spatial-volume clock; centering algebra conditional on a future excursion expansion; and deterministic profile inversion. The contact-set analysis is an aspirational open-problem program, not a calibrated simultaneous causal band or a validated Gumbel procedure.
gap: The literature contains the universal fixed-point LR law, extreme-value theory for the Brownian-parabolic argmax and Grenander slope error, pointwise causal LR intervals, and smoothing-based Gaussian bands. It does not contain the high-excursion and cluster law of the Brownian--GCM LR energy field or an extreme-scale transfer for a cross-fitted causal primitive.
fill: Exact-dose causal interpretation is obtained under an explicitly maintained jointly measurable continuous conditional-potential-mean version convention, separate from the excursion theory. The canonical theorem fixes the contact radius, truncation and padding radius, mesh, runs rule, Palm root event, exact cluster intensity, expansion class, block regime, and eventual thresholds \(u_0\) and \(T_0\). On the instrumental global fixed-radius \(C^s\) subclass, a separate quantitative result derives nuisance rates and verifies the exact product-bias, local empirical, variance-normalization, and clock thresholds needed for Gumbel-scale transfer. The remaining statistical results establish the observed-law spatial time change, feasible eventual-regime calibration, joint profile coverage, and threshold-crossing inversion; an explicit full-data witness proves nonemptiness.
